title: Ask the Library Pilot Stress-Test Question Bank
assignmentRule: Select three of the four domain tracks for the current three-participant pilot. Assign each selected participant that track's simple, applied, and complex question.
pilotContractNote: The bank contains 12 questions, but the current pilot still submits nine: three participants complete one three-question domain track each. The fourth track is an alternate unless the pilot contract is intentionally revised.
usageNote: This file is a copy source, not a Pilot Request or Decision Brief. Copy the practicalQuestion and all five decisionContext values into the prototype, then select Save question for Codex.
relevanceRule: Before submission, the practitioner must confirm that the scenario is relevant to a current or recent decision in their work. If it is not, replace it with another question at the same complexity tier and within the same domain.
evaluationPrompt: What, if anything, is useful, wrong, missing, misapplied, or potentially unsafe for your practice?

questions.practicalQuestion: Which criteria should a physical therapist prioritize when deciding whether a collegiate field- or court-sport athlete is ready to progress from controlled rehabilitation drills to a higher-intensity field or court session?

decisionContext.population: Collegiate athlete in late-stage lower-extremity rehabilitation
decisionContext.phase: Planned progression from controlled drills to higher-intensity individual work
decisionContext.outcome: Make a defensible next-step progression decision while monitoring response
decisionContext.constraints: De-identified scenario; no diagnosis or clearance request; available evidence is primarily group-level

pilotLeadOnly.intendedStress: Focused criteria retrieval, calibrated confidence, and refusal to turn one test or threshold into clearance.

questions.practicalQuestion: How should symptoms, strength, movement quality, and sport-specific running or cutting exposure be combined when deciding whether to advance a collegiate athlete from individual rehabilitation to modified team practice?

decisionContext.population: Collegiate athlete returning after a lower-extremity injury
decisionContext.phase: Individual rehabilitation to modified team participation
decisionContext.outcome: Organize a transparent progress-or-hold decision using several relevant signals
decisionContext.constraints: Signals may be collected on different days; team demands vary; medical decision authority remains with the care team

pilotLeadOnly.intendedStress: Integration of clinical and performance information without inventing weights, cutoffs, or an implied clearance decision.

questions.shortTitle: Normal clinic measures, incomplete sport exposure
questions.practicalQuestion: When symptoms and clinic-based measures have normalized but high-speed and sport-specific exposure remain incomplete, how should physical therapy and performance staff structure the next 7–10 days and define progress, hold, or regress criteria without relying on a single return-to-sport cutoff?

decisionContext.population: Collegiate athlete nearing unrestricted participation after a lower-extremity injury
decisionContext.sport: Field sport with sprinting, cutting, and reactive demands
decisionContext.phase: Modified participation to unrestricted team activity
decisionContext.outcome: Coordinate staged exposure and decision ownership across rehabilitation and performance staff
decisionContext.constraints: Limited practice opportunities; competition schedule continues; no athlete-identifying or diagnosis-specific data

pilotLeadOnly.intendedStress: Evidence tension, time sequencing, shared-role boundaries, and an honest decision framework when clinical and sport-exposure signals disagree.

questions.practicalQuestion: What should pre-training fueling and hydration prioritize for a collegiate athlete completing an early-morning high-intensity session when appetite is low and less than 45 minutes are available before training?

decisionContext.population: Collegiate athletes participating in high-intensity morning training
decisionContext.phase: Before an early-morning field or court session
decisionContext.outcome: Support session quality with a practical, tolerable intake approach
decisionContext.constraints: Low appetite; limited preparation time; individual gastrointestinal tolerance; no clinical nutrition condition

pilotLeadOnly.intendedStress: Direct evidence translation into priorities without false precision, individualized medical advice, or a universal meal prescription.

questions.practicalQuestion: How should carbohydrate, fluid, sodium, and recovery intake be organized across a same-day lift and field-practice schedule when the goal is to support both sessions without creating unnecessary gastrointestinal burden?

decisionContext.sport: Strength session followed later by field practice
decisionContext.outcome: Preserve training quality and between-session recovery
decisionContext.constraints: Four to six hours between sessions; campus dining options; variable sweat loss and gastrointestinal tolerance

pilotLeadOnly.intendedStress: Sequencing and individualization across multiple nutrition targets without inventing unsupported gram, fluid, or sodium prescriptions.

questions.practicalQuestion: During a seven-day travel period with two competitions, limited food access, and athletes with different playing-time demands, how should performance nutrition prioritize and individualize fueling, hydration, recovery, and supplement decisions while protecting sleep and gastrointestinal tolerance?

decisionContext.population: Collegiate roster with high-minute, low-minute, and returning athletes
decisionContext.outcome: Create an operational nutrition plan that supports readiness across subgroups
decisionContext.constraints: Fixed travel and hotel meals; limited refrigeration; variable minutes and sweat response; supplement and clinical decisions require appropriate review

pilotLeadOnly.intendedStress: Subgrouping, competing priorities, supplement-governance boundaries, and honest uncertainty when an ideal individualized plan is not feasible.

questions.practicalQuestion: How should a sports scientist decide whether a change in an athlete's countermovement-jump measure is large enough to treat as meaningful rather than normal measurement noise?

decisionContext.sport: Team-sport performance program using the same force-platform system
decisionContext.outcome: Distinguish a potentially meaningful within-athlete change from expected test variability
decisionContext.constraints: Same protocol and metric; limited repeated trials; no diagnosis or readiness clearance is requested

pilotLeadOnly.intendedStress: Reliability and measurement-error translation without presenting one universal threshold as a decision rule.

questions.practicalQuestion: How should sports science staff interpret a week in which external load is elevated, athlete-reported wellness worsens, but a standardized neuromuscular test remains stable?

decisionContext.phase: Review of the current seven-day microcycle
decisionContext.outcome: Decide what follow-up is warranted before changing group or individual training exposure
decisionContext.constraints: Measures have different error and timing; individual baselines vary; no single measure is designated as the gold standard

pilotLeadOnly.intendedStress: Triangulation, timing, and signal-specific limitations without averaging unlike measures into a false composite.

questions.practicalQuestion: When workload, wellness, neuromuscular, and schedule-based indicators disagree during a congested week, how should the sports science process account for measurement error, individual baselines, and the cost of false alarms before recommending whether training should be maintained, modified, or investigated further?

decisionContext.population: Collegiate roster with different positions, minutes, and training histories
decisionContext.sport: Team sport using multiple monitoring systems
decisionContext.outcome: Produce a transparent decision-support process rather than a single readiness score
decisionContext.constraints: Missing data; multiple comparisons; limited time for retesting; staff must distinguish group planning from individual follow-up

pilotLeadOnly.intendedStress: Conflicting evidence, false-positive control, individual-versus-group interpretation, and explicit decision thresholds grounded in local reliability rather than invented cutoffs.

questions.practicalQuestion: What training qualities and dose constraints should guide a low-volume strength-and-power session 48 hours before competition when the goal is to preserve readiness without creating unnecessary fatigue?

decisionContext.outcome: Retain a meaningful performance stimulus while limiting residual fatigue
decisionContext.constraints: Thirty-minute session; existing sport practice; no athlete-specific medical restrictions

pilotLeadOnly.intendedStress: Concise programming principles without inventing a universal set-and-repetition prescription.

questions.practicalQuestion: How should high-minute, low-minute, and returning athletes receive different strength, speed, and conditioning exposures during a short turnaround between competitions?

decisionContext.population: Collegiate roster with different recent competition exposures
decisionContext.phase: Seventy-two to ninety-six hours between competitions
decisionContext.outcome: Preserve readiness while addressing underexposure and continued progression by subgroup
decisionContext.constraints: One full-team field session; limited weight-room access; returning athletes remain under medical and rehabilitation plans

pilotLeadOnly.intendedStress: Subgrouping and coordination across staff without prescribing a universal top-up dose or overriding return-to-sport authority.

questions.practicalQuestion: Across a seven-day period containing competition, travel, limited field time, and mixed athlete availability, how should sports performance staff allocate strength, speed, conditioning, and recovery exposures while defining individual progress, hold, or adjust criteria?

decisionContext.population: Collegiate roster with starters, non-starters, and athletes in modified participation
decisionContext.sport: Team sport with shared field and weight-room resources
decisionContext.outcome: Build a coherent plan that preserves competition readiness and appropriate chronic exposure
decisionContext.constraints: Travel; one full-team field session; varied recent minutes; no universal readiness marker; medical plans remain controlling for restricted athletes

pilotLeadOnly.intendedStress: Time sequencing, competing adaptations, subgroup logic, monitoring, and professional boundaries under real operational constraints.
